reviewer: assistant inspection of saved outputs, not an independent human adjudication
rubric_history: v1 required full borrower names and space-separated points; it produced formatting false negatives.
v2 accepted distinctive fixture borrower aliases and hyphenated point descriptions.
v3 checks the opening sentence, rejects explicit planning-only responses, and preserves all recorded responses unchanged.
findings: Stage 2/B, stage 3/B and stage 4/A contain planning commentary instead of a completed note.
Stage 3/A describes Silverline PIK without the explicit unchanged/no-stress qualifier required by this rubric.
Stage 4/B starts with a draft-approval heading, so the strict opening-sentence exposure check fails even though exposure follows.
Stage 3/B claims India has eight paired holdings; the measured panel has six paired debt holdings out of seven. This additional accuracy issue is not captured by the four correction checks.
limits: PIK grading requires an explicit qualification, stronger than merely not calling PIK stressful.
Borrower first-name matching is fixture-specific and can be ambiguous on real data.
One sample per stage/task cannot establish causal improvement or general reliability.
Existing system instructions already require citations; do not attribute existing citation compliance to a new correction.
